Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit — quick question on commits vs runtime tweaks

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — really useful. We're lining up an internal review of the Optimize toolkit and I have two quick asks so we can scope a pilot:

1) From a pricing perspective, how should we think about commit bands vs. upfront credits if our workload is highly cache-friendly (80% prefix reuse) but also has long tail requests that benefit from quantization?

2) Any recommended default quantization profiles that balance throughput and hallucination risk for instruction-tuned models? Our ops lead (cc'd) wants something prescriptive to present to procurement.

If you can share a short tiering file or matrix that maps commit bands to expected per-token costs (with batching and KV-cache assumptions), that'd be perfect.

We're aiming to make a decision by end of next week. Can Redwood provide a pilot SOW + pricing sketch?

Appreciate it —
Samir
[OpsWell — Head of ML Platform]
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit: tiering, runtime tradeoffs & pilot commit structure — OpsWell

Hi Samir — great to hear.

Short answers up front:
- Commit bands are the simplest way to secure predictable per-token economics for high-throughput steady-state workloads. For a cache-heavy profile (80% prefix reuse) you can expect effective token cost reductions of ~30–50% vs. cold runs, but that benefit materializes only once the cache footprint and traffic patterns stabilize.
- For quantization, our recommendation for instruction-tuned models is: start with 8-bit symmetric (INT8) for inference on non-sensitive paths, and use mixed-precision (INT8 + FP16 fallback) for the few long-tail sequences where you want to be conservative on fidelity. That keeps throughput high without notable quality regressions in our evals.

I'll attach a short tiering matrix and a one-pager on quantization profiles. Connor — can you add any operational caveats (KV drift, cache TTLs) and confirm the latency implications for OpsWell's 99th percentile target? Marcus — will follow up on suggested commit bands and an initial pricing sketch.

Next step: I'll prepare a pilot pricing sketch + mutual action plan (MAP) and a draft SOW by EOD Tuesday. Does that timeline work for you?

Attachments: OptimizeToolkit_TierMatrix_v2.xlsx, runtime-quantization-summary.pdf

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Samir / Stephanie — quick ops note from the runtime side:

- Cache assumptions: the 80% prefix reuse you mentioned maps to a small working set if prefixes are consistent across requests. We'll want to baseline the KV hit-rate on a 48–72 hour replay to validate. If the hit-rate stays >75%, batching becomes much more efficient and you can lean heavier on commit pricing.
- TTLs & eviction: suggest a rolling TTL of 6 hours for conversational state with explicit TTLs on per-customer namespaces; this avoids cold-cache storms during rollout.
- Latency: with INT8 and our batching knobs, 95th pct latency typically moves ~4–6 ms faster than FP16 on the same hardware for short sequences. The tradeoff is on degraded quality risk for certain generative prompts — recommend adding a small sample-based eval set from OpsWell to validate before broad quant rollout.

If you want, we can run a 1-day replay + microbenchmark on your sample payloads as part of the pilot SOW (low effort — we instrument and report).

Connor O'Brien
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Samir — following up with a concrete pricing sketch and recommended structure:

Proposal (sketch):
- Pilot term: 3 months, non-recurring credits + optional conversion to a 12-month commit.
- Pilot credit ask: $25k in credits to cover replay + 1 small production canary (up to 100M tokens).
- Convert-to-commit bands (annualized) after pilot:
  * Silver: $100k annual commit — approx $0.0009/token (base) — supports modest batching, standard cache assumptions.
  * Gold: $350k annual commit — approx $0.00065/token — includes prioritized burst capacity and conservative quantization profile support.
  * Platinum: $750k+ annual commit — bespoke unit pricing, custom quantization tuning, and extended SLA.

Discount / credits logic: we typically layer a one-time pilot credit plus a conversion bonus (10–20% credit back applied to first quarterly invoice) if the customer converts to Gold+ within 60 days of pilot completion. The exact banding and per-token numbers will adjust based on the replay results (hit rate, average sequence length, RTT distribution).

Next steps: Stephanie to send MAP + SOW; if OpsWell agrees to the pilot credit and replay, we'll prepare a lightweight DocuSign for the pilot SOW and the conversion term sheet. I've included a HubSpot link to the draft deal for internal tracking.

Marcus Lin
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
